subject: MedPath: Cross-border safeguards & DPA annex — supplemental evidence and next steps
messages:
From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@medpath.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medpath.com>, MedPath Legal <privacy@medpath.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: supplemental transfer safeguards & DPA annex items

Neha —

Thanks for the initial questionnaire response. The legal and security teams reviewed the materials and have two follow-up asks so we can close our DPF assessment:

1) A DPA annex with explicit mapping to the EU data protection framework (we need the clause numbers and the technical/organizational measures mapped to each clause).
2) Evidence of cross-border transfer safeguards for EU->US processing: we require either
   - confirmation of an approved EU transfer mechanism (SCCs/DPF) AND the operational controls that ensure equivalence, or
   - if relying on a DPF path, a short write-up of the specific operational mitigations (routing controls, VPC enforcement, KMS boundary, subprocessor list, and data residency options).

Could you provide the DPA annex draft and a short evidence pack (1–3 artifacts) showing the controls above? If you can include a SOC 2 summary and the KMS architecture diagram that would be ideal.

We need this by COB Friday (2028-07-05) to keep the procurement window. Happy to jump on a 30m call if that’s easier.

—Tom
Tom Reilly
Head of Security, MedPath Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@medpath.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: supplemental transfer safeguards & DPA annex items

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide the materials and aim to get an initial bundle to you by EOD Thursday (2028-07-04). Plan below:

- DPA annex draft with clause-level mapping (redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf)
- Transfer mapping matrix (transfer_mapping_matrix.xlsx) that ties data elements to processing flows, subprocessor locations, and applied safeguards
- SOC 2 summary (soc2-summary-2028q1.pdf) and summary notes on our retention & access logging
- Short technical note on KMS/HSM and key custody for customer data (included in the annex appendix)

Open questions for the MedPath team so we can tailor the artifacts:
1) Do you require the EU Commission SCCs enacted into the annex, or are you evaluating the DPF route and need operational evidence only?
2) Any constraints on redacting subprocessor addresses (we can provide zone-level locations if preferred for security reasons).

We can include a single-sheet diagram of our VPC/private deployment options showing traffic egress controls and region pinning. If you want a quick sync, I’m available Thursday morning.

Best —
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: supplemental transfer safeguards & DPA annex items

Looping in the technical mapping we discussed. A couple of clarifications to help with Tom’s ask:

- For EU->US flows we currently support: (a) SCCs with per-customer binding annexes; (b) a DPF-based operational profile where we provide documented mitigations (routing by geography, customer-controlled KMS keys, and optional on-prem/private deployment).
- The transfer_mapping_matrix.xlsx will include three columns: data class, canonical flow, and mitigation controls (e.g., encryption-in-transit, KMS tenancy, KV-cache expiration, region pin).
- On the SOC2 artifact: we will attach the summary PDF and can provide the full report under NDA (DocuSign link if needed).

Action items I’ll take: prepare the technical annex appendix with the KMS diagram, list of subprocessors and their ISO region (not street addresses), and a short paragraph on our runtime routing policies (how requests are routed by region and fallback behavior).

—Marissa
Director, Customer Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Neha/Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Couple of clarifying points from Legal:

- MedPath prefers SCCs in the contract for now, but we are open to reviewing the operational DPF write-up as supplementary evidence. Please include a redlined SCC clause in the annex so our counsel can review language.
- For the KMS ask: we need a short statement confirming whether customer-managed keys are supported for inference artifacts (note: model checkpoints are not in scope, only customer payloads and persistent embeddings). Please detail: key escrow policy, HSM provider (if any), and key rotation cadence.
- Evidence packaging: a 1-page control summary, the DPA annex draft, and the transfer mapping matrix should be sufficient for the next review. If you could also confirm the date of your most recent SOC 2 Type II coverage period that would be helpful (month/year).

If you can get this to us by COB Thursday we’ll keep the procurement timeline intact. Thanks — happy to jump on a call if necessary.

—Tom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@medpath.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: supplemental transfer safeguards & DPA annex items

Tom —

Understood. Final deliverables we will load to the shared Drive by EOD Thursday (2028-07-04):

- redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf (includes redlined SCC clause + clause-level mapping to EU data protections)
- transfer_mapping_matrix.xlsx (data class -> flow -> control mapping)
- control_summary_1p.pdf (one-page control summary covering KMS, routing, subprocessor governance, logging/retention)
- soc2-summary-2028q1.pdf (summary; full report available under NDA)

Quick answers inline to your KMS questions:
- Customer-managed keys: supported for stored embeddings and persistent customer artifacts in our Dedicated and Private offerings. For Hosted API customers we offer a customer KMS integration option (bring-your-own-key) for encryption-at-rest.
- Key escrow: we do not escrow customer-managed keys; keys remain under customer KMS control unless a separate managed-key service is contracted.
- HSM: for our managed KMS integrations we rely on cloud provider HSM (FIPS 140-2/3 depending on provider region).
- Rotation cadence: rotation can be configured by the customer; we recommend a 90–180 day rotation cadence for customer keys.

If MedPath legal wants us to prepare an SCC redline specifically against their internal template, please upload the template to the Drive link and we’ll produce a tracked-changes version.

I’ll attach the initial files for your team to review and we can schedule a follow-up call Friday morning if needed.

Best regards —
Neha Kapoor
